caption_note: The caption does more than restate the figure: it names the sixteen-lane batch, the two fresh H200 processes, the ceiling behind the coarse plateau and the logarithmic ordinate.

0.reason: The figure is published with the evidence fragment's caption, which states the ceiling explicitly ('runs to the solve's 60-update ceiling and 481 reads, at which point the seed read's residual is not reduced at all'), so the plateau is not read alone; a second convergence cue in the figure would duplicate a distinction the caption already carries, and this review is read-only.

findings.summary: The 1e-2 series is plotted from reads_max with no convergence marker, so its ~481-read plateau presents six slices abandoned at the 60-update ceiling as a measured per-slice read cost. Slice 3 of that step (22 reads) is the one coarse slice that converged, and nothing in the picture distinguishes it from the six that did not: a reader without the caption sees reads fall from 480 to 22 and back, not a solve that stopped.

rubric_items.contrast: pass — the axis labels, tick labels and legend entries all render near-black on white and no text sits on a coloured fill or on a plotted line.
rubric_items.data_ink: pass — six polylines and their markers are the only ink inside the axes; no fills, confidence bands or background shading compete with the data.
rubric_items.decoration: pass — the top and right spines are absent, there are no gridlines, no gradient and no background fill; the frameless top legend is the only element that is not data or axis furniture.
rubric_items.label_collision: pass — no label is clipped and none overlaps another or the data: every tick label and both axis titles lie fully inside the 1400x720 canvas, and the legend sits above the axes clear of the plotted series.
rubric_items.legibility: pass — three series are separable at a glance on the log ordinate: the blue flat-at-3 line lies along the bottom, the orange 4->12 rise crosses the 10 tick at slice 6, and the purple series reads as two ~480 plateaus either side of its collapse to 22 at slice 3.
rubric_items.table_form: pass — the point of the evidence is the shape of reads across slice index (the slice-3 dip, the slice-6 rise, the coarse plateau), which reads faster from three lines than from the 21-row per-slice table placed beside it.
